inc.title: Side income ideas
inc.subtitle: Ways students earn on the side, kept by the Campus Coin team — and the source behind each one.
inc.intro: These are ideas, not income promises. Nothing here states what you would earn, how much of your week it would take in your part of the country, or whether it is open to you. It is a short list of ways students have earned on the side, written so you can judge which ones are worth a look.
inc.disclaimer: Orientation only — not financial advice, and not a promise of income. Pay rates, rules and demand change, so check anything that matters before you rely on it.
inc.noSource: No source recorded for this one.
inc.emptyBody: No ideas have been added yet. An administrator curates this list, and it fills in as soon as the first entries go in.
inc.noMatchBody: No idea matches this search and filter combination. Try a shorter search word, or clear the filters to see the whole library.
inc.admin.title: Side income ideas
inc.admin.subtitle: Curate the list students see. Every claim should carry a source — that is what makes it defensible.
inc.admin.emptyBody: Add the first way a student can earn on the side. A short, honest summary is worth more than a long one.
inc.admin.needBoth: Please give the idea a title and a short summary.
inc.admin.summaryHelp: One or two sentences in plain words. No expected amounts — the page must never promise income.
inc.admin.howHelp: Optional. How the work is usually organised, who pays for it and what the hours look like.
inc.admin.effortHelp: Optional. In words, not hours per week — words do not go stale the way a figure does.
inc.admin.effortPh: A couple of evenings a week
inc.admin.startupHelp: Optional, in words. Say when there is nothing to buy.
inc.admin.iconHelp: One emoji, shown on the card.
inc.admin.sourceUrlHelp: Optional on its own. The page where the figure or the trend was read.
inc.admin.sourceNoteHelp: Optional on its own. Name where it came from in words, e.g. the careers newsletter, spring edition.
inc.admin.trendingRule: A trending idea needs a source (URL or note). A badge is a claim about what students are doing now, and it has to say where that was found.
inc.admin.activeHelp: Off keeps the idea out of the public list without losing its source.
inc.admin.orderHelp: Lower numbers come first. Trending ideas are always shown before the rest.
inc.admin.deleteBody: "{name}" comes off the library for good. Retiring it instead keeps the row and its source without showing it to students.
